answer.exemplar: F sharp major is six steps clockwise from C, so the shortest path is six steps in either direction.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: six steps clockwise reaches F sharp major, and six steps counterclockwise is the same distance. On that basis "F sharp major is six steps clockwise from C, so the shortest path is six steps in either…" is the supported choice.

options.text: C is the second degree of D major.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: from D, a whole step reaches E as the second degree. On that basis "E is the second degree of D major" is the supported choice. Thirty-one semitones make that minor nineteenth.
